newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines-Feb 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines-Feb 24.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Security has been tightened around Tiananmen Square in Beijing to prevent unorganised gatherings, and police have detained two people who had guns with them.

-- MING PAO -- In his speech at Deng's funeral on Tuesday President Jiang Zemin will stress Deng's two major contributions: correcting the mistakes of the Cultural Revolution and launching reforms and an open-door policy.

-- SING TAO -- Before Deng died, leftist forces in Beijing drafted a 25,000-word leaflet, attacking the reforms and open-door policy, warning that once the system of socialist state ownership lost its dominant position, the Communist Party would lose the economic foundation of its power.

-- WEN WEI PO -- China's National People's Congress Standing Committee approved a resolution to scrap or amend 14 laws after the Hong Kong handover because they were not considered to be in line with the Basic Law.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- Property development and construction materials group K Wah International has unveiled a proposal to sell its entire construction materials operation to listed subsidiary International Pipe.
-- Chief Executive-designate Tung Chee-hwa is almost certain to pay tax on his salary, as China seeks to distance the territory from its British past. Tung's future income had not been revealed.

-- HONGKONG STANDARD --Chinese leaders were divided over whether to allow two controversial former top-level Communist Party figures to attend Deng's funeral. President Jiang had rejected a request from former party general secretary Zhao Ziyang to attend the funeral, while Deng's family urged that hardliner Deng Liqun, a former propaganda chief and head of the party's most conservative faction, be excluded from the funeral committee.
-- The Preparatory Committee has ruled that neither the post-handover government nor the Provisional Legislature will be able to alter the election rules for electing the first SAR legislature.
